one_liner: Salesforce is a leading enterprise CRM and low-code platform with extensive APIs for data, metadata, automation, analytics, and eventing.
access_notes: Anyone can get a free Developer Edition org and create a Connected App to obtain client ID/secret.
mcp_notes: Salesforce MCP Servers — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_headless360_mcp_servers.htm
blocker_notes: Customer orgs need API access per edition; Professional requires add-on and Connected App admin approval may be needed.

one_liner: Customer platform CRM, Marketing, Sales, Service, CMS, Commerce with extensive public APIs.
access_notes: Create a free developer account to get self-serve app credentials and developer test accounts.
mcp_notes: https://developers.hubspot.com/changelog/hubspot-developer-mcp-server-for-app-and-cms-development-now-in-ga?utm_source=openai

one_liner: Sales-focused CRM for managing leads, deals, contacts, activities and pipelines, with an open REST API and developer platform.
access_notes: Create an app in Developer Hub on a developer sandbox account, then copy client_id and client_secret from the “OAuth & access scopes” tab.
mcp_notes: No official server; third parties have published non‑vendor MCP servers. https://www.reddit.com/r/mcp/comments/1s2bqw7/pipedrive_mcp_server_enables_users_to_manage/
blocker_notes: Public Marketplace listing requires app review; private/unlisted distribution is possible without submission.

one_liner: AI-native, relational CRM with REST API, App SDK, webhooks, and hosted MCP server.
auth_methods: OAuth2; API key; Bearer/PAT token; Basic
access_notes: Self-serve credentials are available (API keys on all plans; OAuth 2.0 auth code flow). However, publishing a public OAuth app for broad distribution requires app review, and unpublished apps are limited to 25 installs. Docs: https://attio.com/help/reference/apps/generating-an-api-key https://docs.attio.com/rest-api/guides/authentication.md https://docs.attio.com/share/the-publication-lifecycle.md
mcp_notes: Official Attio-hosted MCP server (vendor-provided): https://docs.attio.com/mcp/overview.md
blocker_notes: Public app distribution requires Attio App Store review; unpublished apps are capped at 25 workspace installs. See: https://docs.attio.com/share/the-publication-lifecycle.md

one_liner: Modern open-source CRM platform with extensibility as code, REST/GraphQL APIs, and a native MCP server for AI assistants.
access_notes: Cloud self-serve signup with free trial; create API keys under Settings → Developers → API; OAuth flows available without partner review.
mcp_notes: Native MCP server on Cloud.
blocker_notes: After the free trial, Cloud is paid; self-host remains free if users run their own instance.

one_liner: Customizable work platform/CRM by Progress; the API exposes most Podio functionality for apps, items, tasks, search and more.
access_notes: Any user can sign in/sign up and create an OAuth client (API key) in account settings; API is usable on both free and paid accounts within base limits.
mcp_notes: Official vendor MCP server: https://mcp.podio.com

one_liner: Cloud CRM for sales teams to manage leads, deals, automation, and analytics.
access_notes: OAuth clients can be created self‑serve in the API Console.
mcp_notes: Official Zoho CRM MCP server provided by Zoho — https://www.zoho.com/crm/developer/docs/mcp/overview.html

one_liner: Sales CRM with built‑in telephony, email, SMS, automation, and AI for inside‑sales teams.
access_notes: 14‑day free trial; create API keys and OAuth apps in Settings.
mcp_notes: https://mcp.close.com/mcp
blocker_notes: Public OAuth app/listing requires Close review.

one_liner: CRM built for Google Workspace teams; public Developer API for CRM objects and webhooks.
access_notes: Self-serve trial includes API access. API keys are self-serve for admins on eligible plans; OAuth2 apps require emailing partners@copper.com to obtain client_id/client_secret.
mcp_notes: Official MCP server by Copper; announced on copper.com/mcp, with beta/launch targeted for November 2026: https://www.copper.com/mcp?utm_source=openai
blocker_notes: API access is available during the self-serve trial, but production-ready OAuth2 apps require manual client registration via partners@copper.com; ongoing use after the trial typically requires a paid plan.

one_liner: Deal and relationship management platform for financial services.
access_notes: Credentials are provisioned inside a customer tenant by an admin; user enables and copies API key, and some features require account manager enablement.
mcp_notes: Official DealCloud MCP (Celeste license)
blocker_notes: Customers must provision credentials in-tenant; some eventing requires account manager enablement; moderate rate limits and short-lived tokens.

one_liner: Customer support platform with ticketing, help center, messaging, voice, CRM, and robust APIs.
access_notes: Self-create an OAuth client for one Zendesk account; for multi-tenant/public apps you must request a Zendesk-issued global OAuth client via the Marketplace.
mcp_notes: Official MCP client GA; Zendesk MCP server available via Bridge/EAP.
blocker_notes: Global OAuth client requires Marketplace request/approval to ship a multi-tenant toolkit.

one_liner: Customer service platform with AI and a public developer platform.
access_notes: Create a development workspace, then use a workspace Access Token for private apps or set up OAuth for public apps.
mcp_notes: Official Intercom MCP server: https://developers.intercom.com/docs/guides/mcp
blocker_notes: Public, multi-tenant distribution requires Intercom’s app review.

one_liner: Cloud helpdesk for ticketing, knowledge base, automations, and omnichannel customer support.
access_notes: Publish a Marketplace app for cross-tenant OAuth; or use per-account API keys.
mcp_notes: Per-tenant MCP at https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp; API key auth only.
blocker_notes: Multi-tenant OAuth requires Marketplace app review; rate limits vary by plan.

one_liner: Customer operations platform: shared inbox/help desk with multichannel messaging, automation, and AI.
access_notes: Free developer accounts provide a sandbox and allow creating apps, OAuth clients, and API tokens without contacting support.
mcp_notes: https://help.front.com/en/articles/4883136
blocker_notes: You can build and ship an OAuth-based connector today using self-serve developer creds. For broad distribution via Front’s App Store, there’s a partner publishing process and review.

one_liner: B2B‑focused, AI‑powered omnichannel support platform (tickets/issues from Slack, email, chat, portal) with an extensive REST
access_notes: API is available on paid tiers; trials are sales-assisted and require contacting Pylon to set up a demo organization—no self-serve signup for credentials (see pricing page).
mcp_notes: Official vendor-hosted MCP server at https://mcp.usepylon.com; connects via OAuth to a Pylon account.
blocker_notes: API access and trial orgs are provisioned via sales; no self-serve credential issuance.

one_liner: Omnichannel helpdesk with ticketing, live chat, call center, knowledge base, automations, and an API.
access_notes: 30-day free trial, no credit card; API keys available on all plans with per-plan key limits.
mcp_notes: MCP server URL https://<your-liveagent-domain>/api/mcp; supports OAuth 2.1 or bearer token.
blocker_notes: Production use requires a paid plan after trial; API key count and rate limits apply.

one_liner: API-first B2B support platform with full GraphQL API parity to the app.
access_notes: Sign up and start a 7‑day free trial; after trial, a paid plan is required.
mcp_notes: vendor-hosted MCP server at mcp.plain.com; OAuth user auth
blocker_notes: Credentials are self-serve (trial → paid).

one_liner: Email-first help desk with inboxes, live chat, knowledge base, reporting, and apps.
access_notes: Create an OAuth2 app in the UI for Inbox/Chat; Docs API uses user API key via Basic; configure Webhooks in-app.
mcp_notes: mcp.helpscout.net/mcp
blocker_notes: API access requires a paid plan; reporting endpoints gated to Plus/Pro.

one_liner: Ecommerce‑focused helpdesk and AI platform (built for Shopify) that unifies email, chat, social, SMS, and voice support.
access_notes: Any Gorgias account (free 7‑day trial or paid) can generate API credentials; public OAuth apps intended for listing/distribution require Gorgias app review.
mcp_notes: Official vendor MCP for Gorgias, documented by Gorgias and compatible with assistants like Claude and ChatGPT; available on all Helpdesk plans.
blocker_notes: You can build and test immediately (trial + sandbox) and ship OAuth2, but broad multi-tenant distribution/listing in the Gorgias App Store requires app review; customers need an active Gorgias workspace.

one_liner: a customer service/helpdesk platform organized around customer conversations
access_notes: Someone must complete the registration and sign in to Gladly to create API tokens or webhooks.
mcp_notes: https://mcp.us-1.gladly.com/acme/mcp
blocker_notes: Need a live Gladly tenant; no self-serve dev org.
evidence_urls: https://developer.gladly.com/rest/; https://help.gladly.com/docs/generate-api-tokens-and-create-webhooks/; https://developer.gladly.com/rest/; https://developer.gladly.com/rest/; https://developer.gladly.com/rest/; https://help.gladly.com/docs/set-up-the-gladly-mcp-for-claude; https://help.gladly.com/docs/set-up-mcp-connections; https://help.gladly.com/developer-tutorials/docs/request-signing; https://developer.gladly.com/rest/; https://www.gladly.ai/request-demo/

one_liner: Team messaging platform with APIs for bots, automations, and integrations.
access_notes: anyone can create an app and get OAuth client credentials; unlisted distribution is allowed; listing in the Slack Marketplace requires approval.
mcp_notes: Official MCP server and Slackbot MCP client: https://docs.slack.dev/changelog/2026/02/17/slack-mcp
blocker_notes: Marketplace (listed) distribution requires app review; some workspaces restrict installs to Marketplace-only apps.

one_liner: Cloud CPaaS for programmable messaging, voice, email (SendGrid), WhatsApp and related customer engagement APIs.
access_notes: Sign up for a Twilio account (free 30‑day trial); create API Keys or register an OAuth app to obtain tokens.
mcp_notes: Hosted Twilio MCP server (Public Beta) at mcp.twilio.com/docs.
blocker_notes: Paid plan required to move beyond time‑boxed free units and trial restrictions.

one_liner: Team chat and collaboration app with chats, channels, calls, bots, and extensions.
access_notes: Create an OAuth client in Zoho API Console (server-/client-/mobile-/non-browser/self-client). Receive client_id/client_secret, then do standard OAuth 2.0 code flow to get access/refresh tokens.
mcp_notes: Zoho Cliq MCP Server — https://www.zoho.com/cliq/mcp-server.html

one_liner: All‑in‑one workplace suite with chat, docs, calendar, and rich Open Platform.
access_notes: Create apps and get credentials in the Developer Console; public distribution requires ISV certification and platform review.
mcp_notes: “OpenAPI MCP Tool” maintained by Lark connects agents to core Open Platform APIs; supports tenant_access_token and user_access_token. https://open.larksuite.com/document/mcp_open_tools/mcp-user-guide?utm_source=openai
blocker_notes: Public distribution and some scopes require ISV certification/review; internal apps work within a tenant.

one_liner: Team chat and collaboration app with channels, DMs, calls, integrations, and apps platform.
auth_methods: OAuth2; API key; Bot token; HMAC/signature
access_notes: you can self-serve create/install apps and get working credentials; publishing a Public app to the CAKE.com Marketplace requires review.
mcp_notes: Pumble hosts an MCP server to connect agents (Claude, Gemini, etc.) using your app key plus user/bot token; tools map to selected scopes.
blocker_notes: for a public OAuth app listing; private installs are immediate

one_liner: real‑time communications platform (text, voice, video)
access_notes: Create an app in the Discord Developer Portal to self-serve client ID/secret and optional bot token; production scale and privileged intents require passing Discord’s app review/verification.
mcp_notes: Community MCP servers exist; there is no official MCP server from Discord.
blocker_notes: App Verification is required to scale beyond 100 servers; Privileged Intents require review once the app reaches ≥10,000 users, with annual re-review.

one_liner: Cloud-based messaging platform with two main developer surfaces: the HTTPS Bot API for bots/mini apps and the MTProto client API for full-featured clients; plus “Log in with Telegram” for user authentication.
access_notes: Anyone can create a bot and obtain a token via @BotFather; api_id/api_hash for MTProto are issued self-serve at my.telegram.org.
mcp_notes: Community MCP servers exist (often Telethon-based) that enable agents to read/send messages via MTProto or the Bot API; no official vendor MCP.
blocker_notes: None. Credentials are self-serve via @BotFather for the Bot API and my.telegram.org for MTProto; standard bot constraints (can’t initiate user chats, rate limits) exist but don’t block integration.

one_liner: Meta’s enterprise APIs for sending/receiving WhatsApp messages and calls, plus programmatic account and template management.
access_notes: Use Embedded Signup to mint BISU tokens; production, multi-tenant use requires App Review and Advanced access.
mcp_notes: Official Meta MCP server is available: WhatsApp Business Tools MCP at https://mcp.facebook.com/whatsapp_business_tools (docs: https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/mcp).
blocker_notes: Production, multi-tenant use requires App Review and Advanced access for whatsapp_business_messaging and usually whatsapp_business_management.

one_liner: Cloud phone and AI customer communications platform
access_notes: OAuth client ID/secret are issued only after joining the Technology Partner program; while Basic API keys are self-serve for an Aircall customer admin, public/multi-tenant apps must use OAuth per the docs (https://developer.aircall.io/docs/oauth, https://developers.aircall.io/api-references).
mcp_notes: Official Aircall MCP server: https://mcp.aircall.io/mcp (per Aircall docs).
blocker_notes: OAuth credentials require acceptance into Aircall’s Technology Partner program before they are issued.

one_liner: Cloud communications platform with Messaging, Voice, Video, Verify, Numbers, Reports, Network APIs.
auth_methods: API key; Basic; JWT/service account; HMAC/signature; OAuth2
access_notes: Self-serve signup provides an API key/secret and other creds from the dashboard. Live messaging/voice usage may require adding credit or number/brand registration depending on region, but credentials and basic sandbox/testing are self-serve.
mcp_notes: Official Vonage MCP servers: Documentation MCP Server and MCP Tooling Server (per Vonage press release: https://s29.q4cdn.com/651905246/files/doc_news/Vonage-Expands-Developer-Ecosystem-to-Accelerate-the-Next-Era-of-Enterprise-Digital-Transformation-2026.pdf)

one_liner: Google’s advertising platform and API for programmatic management, reporting, and optimization of Google Ads accounts and campaigns.
access_notes: Enable the API on a Google Cloud project and apply for Explorer, then Basic (brand verification) or Standard (review).
mcp_notes: https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/developer-toolkit/mcp-server
blocker_notes: Basic and Standard access require brand verification and typically involve review.

one_liner: Create and manage Meta ads and pull insights via the Marketing API.
access_notes: Create a Facebook app and use OAuth2; production access typically requires App Review and standard-tier access.
mcp_notes: https://mcp.facebook.com/ads
blocker_notes: Production use typically needs App Review for advanced permissions/features and higher quotas.

one_liner: Programmatic access to LinkedIn’s Marketing platform to create/manage ad campaigns, audiences, leads, and reporting across LinkedIn Ads.
access_notes: Access is via the LinkedIn Developer Portal; you must apply for each Marketing/Advertising product and obtain LinkedIn’s review/approval for tier upgrades.
mcp_notes: Community MCP server available: https://github.com/Nuraveda/linkedin-ads-mcp
blocker_notes: LinkedIn Marketing/Advertising APIs require applying for product access and passing LinkedIn’s review (Development -> Standard tiers) before meaningful production use.

one_liner: all‑in‑one marketing automation and CRM platform for agencies and SMBs.
access_notes: You can self‑sign up for a Developer Marketplace account (no manual approval form) and create an OAuth app; a sandbox account is available for developers.
mcp_notes: https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005741-how-to-use-the-highlevel-mcp-server
blocker_notes: Public distribution in the Marketplace goes through an app review process; some higher‑tier endpoints are plan‑gated.

one_liner: Email and marketing automation platform with APIs for audiences, campaigns, and automations.
access_notes: Create an account, generate an API key, and/or register an OAuth app without review.
mcp_notes: Marketing docs MCP: https://mailchimp.com/developer/_mcp/server; Transactional MCP: https://mandrillapp.com/mcp

one_liner: Customer marketing platform for email, SMS, push, and reviews.
access_notes: Any account can create API keys and OAuth apps; new test accounts start on the free plan; free plan is advertised and self-serve.
mcp_notes: Klaviyo publishes an official MCP server (remote-hosted and local) to let AI clients operate on account data with OAuth.
blocker_notes: Marketplace listing requires app review; not needed for unlisted OAuth app.

one_liner: All-in-one marketing platform: funnels, email, automations, courses, products, affiliates.
access_notes: Self-serve: generate API keys in-account under Settings → MCP & API keys (up to 3 keys per account). See https://help.systeme.io/article/2323-how-to-use-systeme-io-public-api
mcp_notes: Official vendor MCP server is built into systeme.io and included on all plans; see https://systeme.io/mcp

one_liner: API v5 for Pins/Boards, ads management/reporting, catalogs, conversions, and analytics.
access_notes: Create/login to a Business account, accept Developer Terms, request Trial (reviewed), then upgrade to Standard (additional review incl. demo video).
mcp_notes: Official Pinterest MCP Server provided by Pinterest: https://developer.pinterest.com/about-pinterest-mcp/
blocker_notes: Production-scale features and higher rate limits require Pinterest app review; some features may need account-team enablement.

one_liner: Meta’s Threads Graph API lets apps post on behalf of a user, retrieve media and profiles, moderate replies, run keyword/profile discovery, and fetch insights.
access_notes: Create a Meta app and select the “Threads” use case; permissions for non‑role users require App Review; webhooks require Live/advanced access and business verification.
mcp_notes: No official MCP from Meta; multiple third‑party/open‑source MCP servers exist that wrap the Threads API.
blocker_notes: Production‑grade usage requires App Review, Live mode/advanced access, and business verification.

one_liner: Twilio SendGrid — cloud email delivery and marketing platform (Email API + Marketing Campaigns)
access_notes: New accounts start on a 60‑day trial; free plans were retired in 2025.
mcp_notes: https://github.com/deyikong/sendgrid-mcp
blocker_notes: Trial expires; ongoing production use requires a paid plan.

one_liner: ecommerce platform with Admin and Storefront APIs to build apps, manage store data.
access_notes: You can self‑serve dev credentials and install on development stores, but public distribution across multiple merchants requires Shopify’s app review and approval.
mcp_notes: Shop MCP (buyer-side, hosted at mcp.shop.com) is available; a separate “Shopify MCP” for merchant‑side Admin actions is announced as “coming soon” in docs.
blocker_notes: Public distribution needs review; some scopes (e.g., protected customer data) need separate approval; Admin APIs are rate‑limited; REST Admin API is legacy (GraphQL required for new public apps as of Apr 1, 2025).

one_liner: Open‑source ecommerce plugin for WordPress with a comprehensive REST API for store management.
access_notes: admins generate keys in each WooCommerce store; no paid tier required for core REST API.
mcp_notes: WooCommerce AI exposes an official MCP server for stores (remote via WordPress.com OAuth, plus optional direct API‑key transport).

one_liner: Open SaaS ecommerce platform with REST/GraphQL Admin and Storefront APIs.
access_notes: You can create API accounts on any store (including trials) and register draft OAuth apps to install on stores you own; to make the app available to other stores, submit it for approval and, for marketplace listing, use a Technology Partner account.
mcp_notes: Official vendor-operated MCP servers: Storefront MCP (GA) and Store Management MCP (early access) by BigCommerce.
blocker_notes: Public distribution requires BigCommerce app review for marketplace listing/installation by other stores; submission typically goes through the Technology Partner program, but you can build and test via draft apps and store-level API accounts without outreach.

one_liner: Enterprise ecommerce platform (formerly Demandware) with headless and traditional storefront options
access_notes: API access is not self‑serve; you must be a Salesforce Commerce Cloud customer (via sales). Account administrators then use Account Manager to create API clients for SCAPI/OCAPI, and on‑demand sandboxes require purchased credits. Docs: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=cc.b2c_account_manager_add_api_client_id.htm&type=5 and https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/b2c-developer-sandboxes.html
mcp_notes: Official Salesforce MCP: @salesforce/b2c-dx-mcp
blocker_notes: Requires being a Salesforce Commerce Cloud customer or approved partner to obtain org access, credentials, and sandboxes; on‑demand sandboxes require purchased credits.

one_liner: E‑commerce platform with Open Source, PaaS, and SaaS options, REST and GraphQL APIs.
access_notes: For Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service, you must go through Adobe Sales/onboarding to obtain access and set up OAuth2 via Adobe IMS/Developer Console. PaaS/on‑prem/Open Source instances can issue admin tokens or OAuth 1.0a integrations locally, but our access classification reflects the SaaS product requiring sales engagement. Docs: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-on-cloud/start/onboarding and https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/webapi/rest/authentication/
mcp_notes: Official Adobe Commerce Developer MCP Server is provided by Adobe (see Commerce developer MCPs and skills in Adobe’s tooling): https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/extensibility/developer-agent/coding-tools
blocker_notes: Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service (SaaS) requires an enterprise contract and onboarding with Adobe IMS/Developer Console before OAuth2 credentials can be issued; per‑organization setup is needed.

one_liner: Website/ecommerce platform with REST Commerce APIs, webhooks, and an official MCP server to integrate stores and build Extensions.
access_notes: OAuth client registration requires submitting a form and review; per‑site API keys are self‑serve inside a site’s dashboard but gated by plan.
mcp_notes: Official Squarespace MCP server endpoint: https://mcp.squarespace.com/mcp
blocker_notes: OAuth client registration requires review/approval before issuance of client credentials.

one_liner: Embeddable ecommerce platform to add a store to existing sites and sell across channels.
access_notes: Register a public app and use OAuth2; API available only for paid stores.
blocker_notes: API works only for merchants on paid plans.

one_liner: hosted commerce for creators to sell digital goods, memberships, and more.
access_notes: In any Gumroad account, go to Settings → Advanced → create an application. No app review or paid plan required for basic API credentials.
mcp_notes: Official vendor MCP server provided by Gumroad: https://gumroad.com/claude/v1/mcp
blocker_notes: Self-serve credentials are available, but the API cannot create products or upload content (creation/upload not supported), and there is no dedicated API sandbox (only test purchases).

one_liner: Amazon’s official REST APIs for sellers/vendors to manage selling operations programmatically.
access_notes: Professional selling account primary user creates a Developer Profile and registers an app to obtain client_id/client_secret; production/public use is subject to Amazon’s app review and role approvals.
mcp_notes: Official Amazon Selling Partner Connector MCP server is hosted by Amazon at https://sellingpartner-ai.amazon.com/mcp (bundled via the amzn/selling-partner-agentic-toolkit).
blocker_notes: Self-serve dev credentials are available, but moving to production requires Amazon’s app review (including restricted role/DPP approval for PII), a Professional selling account, and meeting Appstore listing/onboarding requirements; SQS/EventBridge notifications setup is also required for many use cases.

one_liner: All‑in‑one platform to create, sell, and get paid—checkouts, funnels, communities, webinars, payments.
access_notes: Self‑serve: obtain API keys in the merchant dashboard ("You can find your API key in your merchant dashboard under the API section.") per https://demo.embedded.fanbasis.io/docs/checkout-session-secret; product page advertises REST API, SDKs and a full sandbox at https://commas.com/payments.
mcp_notes: Official vendor MCP in beta from Commas: “Run Commas from your AI assistant…” https://commas.com/
blocker_notes: No blocker: API keys are self‑serve from the merchant/seller dashboard and public docs mention REST API and a sandbox.

one_liner: pay‑as‑you‑go SEO data APIs (SERP, keywords, backlinks, on‑page, business data)
access_notes: Create a free account with DataForSEO, then go to the API Access tab in the account dashboard to find your API login and password.
mcp_notes: https://github.com/dataforseo/mcp-server-typescript

one_liner: All-in-one SEO platform with Data and Project APIs.
access_notes: 14‑day standalone API trial with 100,000 free credits.
mcp_notes: https://api.seranking.com/mcp
blocker_notes: Beyond trial/included credits, sustained use requires buying credits; rate limits apply.

one_liner: SEO/AEO data platform with a public REST API and hosted MCP server.
access_notes: Partner-gated: you must apply and be approved for Ahrefs Connect to obtain OAuth client credentials; API keys are available only to approved/eligible paid accounts. Docs: https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/api/docs/introduction and OAuth guide: https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/ahrefs-connect/docs/oauth-guide.
mcp_notes: Official Ahrefs-hosted MCP server (vendor-operated): https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/mcp/docs/introduction (available to Lite plan or higher).
blocker_notes: API access requires acceptance into Ahrefs Connect/partner program before credentials are issued; additionally, eligibility is limited to paid plans with quota limits (uncapped access on Enterprise).

one_liner: AI-powered web scraping platform with a Scraper API, a Platform API to create/rerun/manage scrapers and results, marketplace endpoints, web search, proxies, and webhooks.
access_notes: Self-serve signup provides a 7‑day trial (e.g., 1,000 tokens) but a credit card is required to start the trial per pricing/docs.
mcp_notes: Official MrScraper MCP: managed hosted MCP endpoint using OAuth 2.1 consent flow, with an accompanying open‑source server (see https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server).

one_liner: Hosted web‑scraping and automation platform; you run “Actors” via a REST API and fetch structured results from storages.
access_notes: free signup yields API tokens; free monthly credits, no card
mcp_notes: vendor‑hosted server at https://mcp.apify.com with OAuth or bearer token auth; also a local stdio server and official GitHub repo

one_liner: Web data API for AI agents to search, scrape, crawl, map, parse and interact with the live web, returning clean Markdown or structured JSON; official MCP server included.
access_notes: Self-serve: free tier with 1,000 monthly credits; keyless basic calls also allowed.
mcp_notes: Hosted MCP at mcp.firecrawl.dev with OAuth or API key modes.

one_liner: Web data platform providing web scraping APIs, Browser API, proxy networks, datasets.
access_notes: An API key… We create a default key for you upon account creation automatically.
mcp_notes: https://docs.brightdata.com/products/mcp-server/overview

one_liner: Open‑source CLI that hunts down social media accounts by username across 400+ sites.
blocker_notes: No hosted API; CLI/local tool only.

one_liner: Unified B2B contact/company intelligence API that aggregates 30+ vendors for prospecting, enrichment (emails, phones), job-change checks, company reveal, and email verification.
access_notes: Authenticate … with your Waterfall API key in the x-api-key header. Contact the team (support@waterfall.io) for API access and pricing.
blocker_notes: Developers must talk to sales to obtain a key (no self-serve signup flow exposed).

one_liner: GTM data platform to find, enrich, and activate leads with AI and workflows.
access_notes: Generate a Clay API key in-app or via CLI; the developer platform is available on all plans including free, and MCP registration is open with no approval required.
mcp_notes: Official Clay-operated MCP server; connect by registering your platform as an OAuth client (open registration, no Clay-side approval).

one_liner: Code hosting and collaboration with REST and GraphQL APIs for automation and integrations
auth_methods: OAuth2; Bearer/PAT token; JWT/service account; Basic
access_notes: Credentials are self‑serve: any user/org admin can register OAuth apps or GitHub Apps in settings; no paid plan or partner gating to start.
mcp_notes: https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server

one_liner: Frontend cloud for building, deploying, and operating web apps.
access_notes: Self-serve: create a Personal Access Token from Account Tokens or set up an OAuth integration to get client ID/secret. Marketplace listing and broader distribution may require review, but basic credentials do not.
